findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State concretely how the just-archived tail-fold happens (e.g. `rebar archive` performs a final fold inline, or name/verify the scheduled `--include-archived` sweep) and add an acceptance criterion proving no events are stranded unfolded after archival under the new default.
evidence: 'a final fold for a just-archived ticket still happens via the scheduled sweep run with --include-archived (documented), so no events are ever stranded unfolded'
No Scope bullet or AC provisions or verifies a scheduled sweep; the plan only adds the flag to on-demand commands.
findings.finding: The plan relies on a 'scheduled sweep run with --include-archived' to fold a just-archived ticket's tail events, but never establishes that such a scheduled sweep exists, who runs it, or its cadence — it is asserted, not specified, and no acceptance criterion covers it.
findings.location: Approach — 'a final fold for a just-archived ticket still happens via the scheduled sweep run with --include-archived (documented)'
scenarios: A ticket is archived with unfolded tail events; default compact-all no longer visits it; if no scheduled --include-archived sweep is actually configured, those events stay unfolded indefinitely.
findings.suggested_fix: Either fold inline at archive time (so default active-only compact-all never needs to reach archived tickets), or specify the scheduled sweep's owner/cadence and add an AC asserting a just-archived ticket's events are fully folded after the documented sequence.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the compact-all default-flip's write-side safety explicitly (guarantee archived tickets are already fully folded, or fold inline at archive) and note the back-out (default reverts to full walk) so the durability guarantee is verified, not asserted.
evidence: 'Switch the fsck scan loops and the compact-all sweep to it'
compact-all performs folds (writes SNAPSHOT); skipping a ticket that still has unfolded events is a durability concern.
No back-out plan is stated; --include-archived is the forward escape hatch but the default-flip's fold guarantee is asserted, not verified.
findings.finding: This is a behavior change to two existing commands (fsck, compact-all no longer visit archived tickets by default), and the write-side command (compact-all folds) skipping archived tickets could leave a just-archived ticket's events unfolded — but the plan provides no rollback/back-out note and its mitigation for the write path is the unproven scheduled sweep.
scenarios: Operator relies on `compact-all` to fold everything; after the default flip a recently archived ticket's tail events are silently not folded until someone remembers --include-archived.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC exercising the archive→default-compact-all sequence and asserting the archived ticket carries no unfolded events; document that reverting the default restores the full walk as the back-out path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a non-CI trigger for the final fold of just-archived tickets (operation-linked fold at archive time, or an in-process fallback), or clarify that `rebar archive` already performs the terminal fold so the scheduled sweep is not load-bearing for correctness in no-CI venues.
evidence: 'a final fold for a just-archived ticket still happens via the scheduled sweep run with --include-archived (documented), so no events are ever stranded unfolded'
Supported venue matrix includes 'projects with NO CI provider at all'; a scheduled sweep whose only trigger is a CI schedule never fires there
findings.finding: The plan makes default fsck/compact-all skip archived tickets and relies on 'the scheduled sweep run with --include-archived' as the mechanism that performs the final fold for a just-archived ticket, but names no non-CI trigger for that scheduled sweep; in a venue with no CI provider the sweep never fires and trailing post-archive events are never folded — contradicting the plan's own claim that 'no events are ever stranded unfolded.'
findings.location: Approach — 'a final fold for a just-archived ticket still happens via the scheduled sweep run with --include-archived (documented)'
scenarios: A developer workstation or a project with no CI provider archives a ticket; because default active-only now excludes it from fsck/compact-all and the 'scheduled sweep' that would fold it never runs, the ticket's trailing events remain unfolded indefinitely and a later deep audit finds unfolded state that the plan promised could not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Have `rebar archive` perform the terminal fold as part of the archive operation itself (operation-linked), so default active-only scoping never strands events regardless of whether any scheduled sweep runs; document the sweep as redundant belt-and-suspenders rather than the sole fold path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Close the just-archived fold gap: either scope compact_trigger.py / the scheduled workflow to run one --include-archived sweep (add them to Scope), or have `rebar archive` fold on its way out, so an archived ticket's log is provably folded and 'no events are ever stranded unfolded' holds.

findings.location: Approach — 'a final fold for a just-archived ticket still happens via the scheduled sweep run with --include-archived (documented), so no events are ever stranded unfolded'
scenarios: A ticket is archived; its event log is above the fold threshold; the scheduled/operation-linked sweep runs with its default (active-only) scope and never selects it

findings.finding: The plan asserts that a just-archived ticket's final fold 'still happens via the scheduled sweep run with --include-archived (documented), so no events are ever stranded unfolded' — but no scope item establishes or configures that scheduled --include-archived sweep, and no acceptance criterion verifies that archived-but-unfolded tickets actually get folded once compact-all defaults to active-only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scope line + AC: e.g. 'a ticket archived with unfolded events is folded on the next --include-archived sweep' with a test that archives a ticket mid-events, runs compact-all --include-archived, and asserts the SNAPSHOT now covers those events; and cite the scheduler/cron entry that runs it.

evidence: leaf.py:173-174 appends ARCHIVED event + write_marker with no compaction — archive does not fold

findings.finding: The plan's mechanism guarantee 'no events are ever stranded unfolded' rests on a rationale that is factually wrong and on an unforced operator assumption: `leaf.archive` (src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py:142) writes only an ARCHIVED event + `.archived` marker and does NOT fold inline, so an archived ticket is NOT 'already folded on its way out' — the only fold is compact-all.
